newsitem.title: UK: Middle East tanker rates flat, Asian demand high.
newsitem.headline: Middle East tanker rates flat, Asian demand high.

text.p: Middle East crude tanker rates were little unchanged on Wednesday, with very large crude carriers (VLCCs) to Japan remaining at W67.5 and to the west and to Singapore at about W55, brokers said.
"There's still much more interest Mideast/east and Mideast/west," one broker said.

Million-barrel vessels on transatlantic trips were livelier. "A million barrels are being fixed at up to W95. That seems to be the perkiest long-haul sector today," the broker said, noting that W87.5 was a typical rate on Tuesday.
VLCCs across the Atlantic remained at about W62.5.
Cross-Med million-barrel vessels rose sharply to W95-97.5, up from about W85. "There were six or seven new cargoes on the market yesterday," an Italian broker said, explaining the rise.
But he said 80,000 tonne cargoes were unchanged at W100, while inter-U.K./Cont rates were flat at W102.5/105.

In the Caribbean, 70,000 tonners to the U.S. Gulf were fixed higher at W170 from W162.5-W165. "A couple of people got caught out on cancellations...Everyone is fixing fairly close. The furthest out date I've seen in the 27th," a U.S. broker said.
Caribs/USAC 50,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes were little changed at W200, he added.
